findings.title: Cancellation of workflow reminders is fire-and-forget and not awaited before the handler returns
findings.body: The forEach loop calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` without awaiting the returned promises, and these calls are not included in the subsequent `Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))`. Previously, the actual DB deletion of the WorkflowReminder was performed via an awaited `Promise.all` so it was guaranteed to complete before the API response was sent. Now, the deferred-cancellation path relies on an async DB update (`cancelled: true`) inside `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` that is never awaited. In a serverless/Next.js API route, the function execution can be frozen or terminated right after the response is returned, meaning this update may never actually run. If it doesn't run, the reminder keeps `cancelled: null/false` and will still be sent out by the `scheduleEmailReminders` cron, which is exactly the regression this PR is supposed to fix.

findings.title: Rescheduling still uses immediate SendGrid cancellation instead of the new deferred-cancellation mechanism
findings.body: When rescheduling, previous workflow reminders are cancelled via `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)` with `immediateDelete=true`, which performs an immediate SendGrid 'scheduled_sends' cancel POST request synchronously (same mechanism described as the root cause of the original bug: too many pending cancellations accumulating and failing once the 100-pending-cancellation quota is hit). Unlike `handleCancelBooking.ts`, which now defers cancellation (sets `cancelled: true` and lets the cron job cancel close to send time), the reschedule flow does not benefit from this fix. Since the PR title explicitly claims to fix reminders for both cancelled AND rescheduled bookings, this inconsistency means the rescheduled-booking scenario can still hit the same SendGrid pending-cancellation limit and fail to cancel stale reminders.

findings.title: A single failed SendGrid cancellation aborts cleanup of the entire cancellation batch
findings.body: The for-loop over `remindersToCancel` performs the SendGrid cancel request and queues a DB delete for each reminder, but the whole loop (and the trailing `await Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)`) is wrapped in one try/catch. If the SendGrid request throws for any single reminder (e.g. transient network error, invalid/expired batch id), the exception propagates out of the loop immediately: remaining reminders in the batch are never processed in this run, and even reminders successfully cancelled with SendGrid earlier in the loop never get their DB delete executed (since `Promise.all` is never reached). This can cause workflow reminders to remain in a 'cancelled but not cleaned-up' state indefinitely if the failure recurs, and prevents other, unrelated reminders scheduled in the same cron tick from being cancelled at all this cycle.

findings.title: remindersToCancel query lacks a method filter for EMAIL reminders
findings.body: The query `prisma.workflowReminder.findMany({ where: { cancelled: true, scheduledDate: {...} } })` does not filter by `method: WorkflowMethods.EMAIL`. This endpoint (scheduleEmailReminders) subsequently treats every returned reminder's `referenceId` as a SendGrid `batch_id` and issues a SendGrid cancel request. If an SMS reminder (or any future reminder type) is ever marked `cancelled: true`, this cron job would incorrectly attempt to SendGrid-cancel it using a non-SendGrid reference id (e.g. a Twilio SID), causing an API error and, per the adjacent bug, potentially blocking cancellation of other legitimate email reminders in the same batch.

findings.title: Unrelated UI refactor bundled into a backend bug-fix PR
findings.body: This file's changes (merging the phone-number/sender-id blocks and removing the outer `(isPhoneNumberNeeded || isSenderIdNeeded)` wrapper) are a UI refactor unrelated to the stated purpose of the PR (fixing workflow reminders for cancelled/rescheduled bookings). While the change itself appears benign (it removes an effectively-empty wrapper div when only `isSenderIdNeeded` is true), bundling unrelated UI changes into a critical bug-fix PR makes the change harder to review and increases the risk of unintentionally introducing a UI regression that isn't covered by this PR's testing focus.

findings.title: No automated tests cover the new deferred-cancellation / cron cancellation logic
findings.body: This PR fixes a previously-reported production bug (workflow reminders still sent after cancellation/reschedule) by introducing a new `cancelled` flag and a batch cancellation step inside the `scheduleEmailReminders` cron job. No tests were added to verify that: (1) reminders marked `cancelled` within the 1-hour window are actually cancelled and removed, (2) a failure in one cancellation does not silently prevent cancellation of other reminders in the same run, or (3) the end-to-end flow (cancel booking -> cancelled flag set -> cron cancels in SendGrid) behaves as expected. Given this is explicitly fixing a reported bug, lack of regression tests risks the same issue resurfacing undetected.
